metadata.metric: E(1%, 1cm) — absorbance of 1% w/w solution at 1 cm path length
metadata.alternative_metric_inorganic: Calibrated effective E(1%, 1cm) equivalent — extrapolated from manufacturer film attenuation data; not a true molar coefficient because particulates do not have a meaningful molarity.
metadata.rendering_notes: Data points are tuples [wavelength_nm, E_value]. Curves are rendered by linear interpolation between points. Where data is sparse, points come from peer-reviewed papers or manufacturer datasheets cited in spectra-verification-*.md.

confidence_codes.C1: primary peer-reviewed paper with full digitised spectrum / multiple ε(λ) points
confidence_codes.C2: primary peer-reviewed / pharmacopoeia / SCCS — peak ε confirmed; shape Gaussian
confidence_codes.C4: digitised approximately from a published figure
confidence_codes.C5: parametric Gaussian fallback; no detailed spectrum located

calibration_notes: ZnO (idx 29) recalibrated 2026-05-07 — peak E1% 9800 → 160 (60× correction); see research/calibration/zno-deep-dive.md
TiO2 (idx 30) recalibrated 2026-05-07 — peak E1% 12500 → 600 (21× correction); see research/calibration/tio2-deep-dive.md
metadata.concentration_nonlinearity_doc: Inorganics use f(c) = 1 - α × tanh(max(0, c-c0)/scale) to model aggregation + film-density saturation at high loading. Per-filter params live in filter.concentration_nonlinearity. Validated to <30% mean SPF error on real formulations.

1.notes: Trans-OMC in EtOH; cinnamate band. Shape Gaussian about λmax 309 nm. Tail extended past 340 nm; cinnamate red-side asymmetric decay.

2.source: Tan-Sien-Hee 2020 PCCP D0CP02610G; ACS Omega 2025 5c09234; DSM PARSOL EHS

3.notes: Salicylate; figure 1 of Stavros 2020 anchors λmax 307–309 nm.

4.notes: Cyanodiphenyl-acrylate; broad band 290–360 nm, λmax 303 nm. Tail extended past 340 nm; cyanoacrylate decay.

5.notes: Cinnamate ester analogue of EHMC; near-identical chromophore.

6.notes: p-aminobenzoate band, λmax 283 nm in EtOH.

7.notes: DMA-PABA push-pull chromophore; ε widely cited 27,000–30,000. Tail extended past 340 nm; PABA push-pull asymmetric decay.

9.notes: Per-chromophore ε; bulk-polymer E(1%,1cm)=160–190 at 312 nm.

10.source: BASF Uvinul T 150 PRD 30035119; Stein 2014 PPS
10.notes: C3-symmetric triazine; E(1%,1cm)≈1500 at 314 nm. Tail extended past 345 nm; triazine narrow band decay.

11.source: ScienceDirect Topic 4-MBC (E1%/1cm = 954 at 300 nm); MDPI Cosmetics 2023
11.notes: Rigid benzylidene-camphor; minimal solvatochromism. Tail extended past 335 nm; benzylidene camphor narrow band decay.

12.source: Symrise Neo Heliopan E1000 (E(1%,1cm) min. 980 at 308 nm in MeOH)
12.notes: Cinnamate ester isomer of EHMC; same chromophore.

13.source: Mol 2021 Phenolic Absorption Coefficients; FDA OTC monograph 21 CFR 352
13.notes: Salicylate anion in water; ε ≈ 3,800 (salicylic acid 300 nm reference). Tail extended past 330 nm; salicylate sharp UVB cutoff.

14.notes: Enol band in MeOH; keto band ~265 nm with ε≈28,400 (added). Tail extended 410-440 nm based on Mturi & Martincigh 2008 figure.

15.source: Cantrell & McGarvey 2000 JPP-B 55:92 (ε=5,800 at 338 nm in EtOH)
15.notes: Anthranilate ester; broad asymmetric band, weak ε. Tail extended to 410 nm based on Cantrell & McGarvey 2000 figure.

16.notes: ESIPT-stabilised hydroxybenzoyl benzoate; very broad band. Tail extended 400-435 nm based on Wang 2023 PPS spectrum.

17.source: Naumov, Herzog, Abel 2020 JPCA 124:247; BASF Tinosorb M PRD 30075
17.notes: Dual peak 305 + 360 nm; aqueous dispersion of <200 nm particles. Tail extended past 405 nm based on Naumov 2020 monomer/dispersion figure.

18.notes: Bis-triazine; very narrow strong UVB band. Tail extended past 355 nm based on 3V Sigma Uvasorb HEB datasheet shape.

19.source: BASF Tinosorb S PRD 30481068; Chatelain & Gabard 2001 PP 74:401
19.notes: Dual peak 310 (UVB) + 343 (UVA-II); E(1%,1cm)≈870@310, 800@343 (BASF). Tail extended past 390 nm based on Chatelain & Gabard 2001 spectrum.

20.source: Deflandre & Lang 1988 IJCS 10:53 (ε=47,000 at 345 nm); Damiani reviews
20.notes: Bis-camphor sulfonate; whole-molecule ε; narrow UVA-II band. Tail extended past 380 nm based on Deflandre & Lang 1988 spectrum.

21.notes: Dual peak 303 + 344 nm; ESIPT benzotriazole. Tail extended past 380 nm; ESIPT benzotriazole sharp red-side decay.

22.source: Marionnet 2021 JID Innov 2:100070 (ε=63,000 at 385 nm); SCCS/1605/19
22.notes: Cyclic merocyanine charge-transfer chromophore, narrow band centred at 385 nm. Symmetric Gaussian shape (σ ≈ 11 nm). Tail extended to 460 nm so visible decays smoothly to near-zero.

23.source: Naumov, Herzog, Abel 2023 PPS 22:2143 (ε≈80,000 at 310 nm); BASF Tinosorb A2B
23.notes: Tris-biphenyl triazine monomer; UVB peak with UVA-II shoulder ~340 nm. Tail 365-415 nm extended based on Naumov 2023 PPS monomer figure.

24.source: Symrise Neo Heliopan AP (E(1%,1cm)≈770–800 at 335 nm)
24.notes: Disodium tetrasulfonate; rigid bis-benzimidazole; narrow band. Tail extended past 370 nm based on Symrise Neo Heliopan AP datasheet.

25.notes: Dual peak 287 (UVB) + 325 (UVA-II); ε(287)≈16k, ε(325)≈13k. Tail extended past 355 nm; BP-3 visible-side decay.

26.notes: Sulfonate of BP-3; aqueous dual peak 286 + 324. Tail extended past 355 nm; BP-4 visible-side decay.

27.notes: Dual peak 282 + 325; second OH red-shifts UVA peak. Tail extended past 365 nm; BP-8 visible-side decay.

28.source: Estimated by analogy to BP-3 (no primary spectrum located)
28.notes: BP-10 nearly obsolete; spectrum extrapolated from BP-3. Tail extended past 355 nm by analogy to BP-3 (C5).

29.source: US20060228310 (Croda) — patent specifying E_max = 12-20 L/g/cm, most preferred 15-16; Patent E360 = 11-20 L/g/cm (most preferred 13.5-14.5), E308 = 11-20 (most preferred 12.5-13.5)
29.notes: Recalibrated from real published k(λ) per Croda US20060228310 patent + Egerton & Tooley 2012 + Cole 2016. Peak E1% = 160 (vs prior parametric value 9800 — ~60× overestimate). Concentration nonlinearity: f(c) = 1 - 0.70 × tanh(max(0, c-2)/10), validated to 22% mean SPF error on 9 mineral formulations.

concentration_nonlinearity.model: f(c) = 1 - alpha * tanh(max(0, c - c0) / scale)
concentration_nonlinearity.rationale: Captures aggregation + film-thickness density effect at high ZnO loading. f(0..2%)=1.0, f(20%)=0.36, f(25%)=0.31. Anchored to industry SPF/% benchmark (1.4 to 2.8).
concentration_nonlinearity.source: Fitted to (a) Sunscreen Co 2024 industry analysis 1.4-2.8 SPF/%, (b) Badger/ThinkSport/Aveeno labelled in-vivo SPFs at 20-25% ZnO, (c) Hupel et al. 2024 PPSci on density-induced film-thickness effect

30.source: Egerton & Tooley 2012 IJCS 34:117 — Mie-theory + measurements; 50 nm rutile k(310 nm) ≈ 60-80 L/g/cm; Popov et al. 2005 J Phys D 38:2564 — Mie-theory optimum 62 nm at 310 nm; 122 nm at 400 nm
30.notes: Recalibrated from real published k(λ) per Egerton & Tooley 2012 + Popov 2005 + SCCS/1516/13 + BASF/Croda datasheets. Peak E1% = 600 at 310 nm (vs prior parametric value 12,500 — ~21× overestimate). Concentration nonlinearity gentler than ZnO (α=0.62 vs 0.70). Validated to 28.9% mean SPF error on 8 mineral formulations.

concentration_nonlinearity.model: f(c) = 1 - alpha * tanh(max(0, c - c0) / scale)
concentration_nonlinearity.rationale: Captures aggregation + Mie-saturation + film-thickness density effect at high TiO2 loading. f(0..2%)=1.0, f(10%)=0.56, f(15%)=0.46, f(20%)=0.41, f(25%)=0.38. Lower alpha than ZnO because TiO2 (a) is less dense (4.23 vs 5.61 g/cm^3) so film thinning is milder, and (b) cosmetic TiO2 is invariably better-coated (alumina+silica) so steric stabilisation suppresses aggregation more.
concentration_nonlinearity.source: Fitted to 8 pure-TiO2 + Ti/Zn-blend product labels (Goddess Garden, Babo, Badger, Blue Lizard, California Baby, Beautycounter); cross-checked vs Croda Solaveil 2-3 SPF/% rule and Sunscreen Company TiO2 1.8-2.6 SPF/% benchmark.

31.notes: Parent 2,4-dihydroxybenzophenone; classic dual peak. Tail extended past 355 nm; BP-1 visible-side decay similar to BP-3.

32.source: Marusak 1980 JPCS 41:981; Sherman & Waite 1985 Am Min 70:1262
32.notes: Hematite Eg≈2.1 eV; d-d bands at 535+650 nm; LMCT dominates UV/blue.

33.source: Sherman & Waite 1985; Scheinost 1999 CCM 47:156; Morris 1985 JGR
33.notes: Goethite Eg≈2.5 eV; bands at 425/500 nm; weaker LMCT than hematite.

34.notes: Magnetite Fe2+/Fe3+ inverse spinel; Eg≈0.2 eV; nearly flat across UV-VIS-NIR.

35.notes: 3-BC parent; analogue of 4-MBC, banned in EU since 2015.

36.source: Sigma-Aldrich product 97085; analogous to 3-BC (no primary spectrum)
36.notes: Water-soluble sulfonate analogue of 3-BC; same chromophore.
